sections.markdown:
## B — Audience and scope

Audience: first-time Hawaii class three applicants, including minors on the graduated path, learning how bad driving habits form from laziness, impatience, inattention, arrogance and ignorance, distracted driving, the five rules of defensive driving, attentiveness and scanning, driver and vehicle condition, trip planning, warning lamps, safety belts, what happens in a collision and protecting a baby in the car in plain English.

Prerequisites: the attitude themes of the driver chapter and the belt and child restraint law from the equipment chapter, which this section explains in practice.

Scope note: the five causes of bad driving habits with their examples, distracted driving including stereos, headsets, phones and pets, the five rules of defensive driving, attentiveness and scanning, driver and vehicle condition, trip planning, warning lamps, the four protections of safety belts and their numbers, belt fit, child seats, the human collision timeline and the baby-in-the-car poster. Backing, lane and speed techniques follow in the next section.

Recall emphasis: the five causes, the five defensive rules, the belt numbers and the lamp meanings are practiced as recall items; no scenario or recognition surface is needed for this section.

corpus_stability.reason: The Hawaii Driver's Manual is a periodically reprinted reference (imprint HMG 5/2023, copyright line through 2023); the how bad driving habits form from laziness, impatience, inattention, arrogance and ignorance, distracted driving, the five rules of defensive driving, attentiveness and scanning, driver and vehicle condition, trip planning, warning lamps, safety belts, what happens in a collision and protecting a baby in the car rules on pages 57–63 are statutory and procedural content that changes less than once a year, so no BlockedProbe.
